classes.title: Fall Intensive Part 1 November 9 - 13
classes.description: Annoyance 2026 Fall Intensives 5 day course - 6 hours per day with additional 2 hour workshops PART 1: The Annoyance Training Center teaches students how to develop and maintain a strong individual voice in their improvisation. These intensives will address the initiation of a scene; developing and maintaining strong characters; learning to hold on to your initial choices while at the same time, expanding on (heightening) the choices you have made; and learning to become deft at creating and weaving unexpected, character-based choices into your work. Annoyance classes challenge the conventional wisdom of the rules of improvisation, examining what’s behind them and how they came to be in the first place. Simply put, we make you the best improviser YOU can be. All of our intensive teachers are ensemble members who have learned and performed with The Annoyance, and thus have first hand experience with the way we approach improvisation. PART 2: Took the Intensive Part 1 and want more? Want to go further with your exploration of our philosophy? This is for you! With this intensive sequel, we go deeper into the teachings of The Annoyance, tackling things like context, group scene work, ensemble and much more. If you can only take one week, take part 1 . In The Annoyance Intensives, we try to cover all of the information in The Annoyance's AP1-5 program each day - AP1 on Monday, AP2 on Tuesday, and so on. These classes meet for 20 hours over 8 weeks. In these intensives, we're trying to cram that info into 6 hours over one day. A truly impossible task. So, part 2 was created as a way to convey more of the information we couldn't get to in part 1, while also allowing instructors to get deeper into concepts they're passionate about, knowing the students all have at least part 1 under their belt. PREREQUISITE FOR PART 2: Students must have previously completed an Annoyance Part 1 Intensive or have completed AP5 within The Annoyance Training Center SCHEDULE: Classes: Mon - Fri 10am-5pm with a 1 hour break for lunch (1-2pm) Optional Workshops: Mon - Thu 5-7pm Optional Showcase: Fri 6pm PAST PART 1 WORKSHOPS: Advanced Improv with Mick Napier Game-Based Improv with Face Off Unlimited (FOU) Musical Improv with Tuesday Musical Improv (TMI) Genre-Based Improv with Hitch*Cocktails Please Disregard Dates and Schedule Listed Below (Those pertain to our non-intensive classes)

Drop-In: Intro to Clown Class: Hannah Mitchell (Tuesday, November 10th, 2026)
classes.description:
“It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

What happens in a clown class? We introduce ourselves, we have a nice long warmup, our feet get squishy and our heads get floaty, we play with tennis balls and hats, we do group games and solo exercise from some of the greats (Lecoq, Conway, Johnstone) while working on taming their ego and bringing out their true inner clown. Come to just one class, come to all of them, do what your heart desires. You’ll probably leave with a new friend.

We're in an era of cognitive dissonance, hence all this clown talk. Absurd times call for an absurd response. Clown is antifascist and you are brave!

Drop-In: Intro to BCC Improv w/ Andy Junk (Thursday, November 12th, 2026)
classes.description:
This Intro class teaches you what the BCC’s approach to improv is all about - how to say both FUCK IT and LOVE IT while performing. FUCK IT means you don’t worry about the outcome or result of your efforts. You are not judging whether you perform things correctly or whether you make mistakes. You are simply committed to doing what you are doing without worrying whether it is good or not. LOVE IT means you celebrate the whimsy, joy, and delight inherent in making shit up onstage. You remember why you fell in love with improv, one of the most wonderful feelings in the world. Learn to hold both of these ideas in your head at the same time and create fearless, fun, and dumb improv.

If you are new to improv, this workshop will set you up for a fearless way to begin learning. If you are an experienced improviser, this workshop will introduce you to a new philosophy of improv that is different than other improv schools in NYC. Either way you will be challenged and motivated!

This class is designed for students new to BCC’s approach to improv.

classes.title: How to Write a Short Humor Piece with Caitlin Kunkel
classes.description: Do you want to write funny in 750 words or less? Do you have something to say on a topic you know well? Do you crave fun, need an outlet for your creativity, and hunger for more bylines? Then, short humor is for you. In this two-hour class, writer and comedy craft book author Caitlin Kunkel will teach a repeatable process for writing a short humor piece in the style of McSweeney’s Internet Tendency, The Belladonna, Points in Case, and other online sites (note: we will not cover satirical news like The Onion or Reductress). You’ll learn how to brainstorm, find a structure for your piece, craft a strong comedic premise and title, and use the two-list system of joke writing to fast draft a humor piece. Come ready to write and leave with a new piece and a set process to write even more in the future. All participants will receive a copy of Inside Jokes: A Comedy and Creativity Guide For All Writers. ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR: Caitlin Kunkel is a writer, teacher, and speaker whose work has been featured in The New Yorker, McSweeney’s, on public radio, and across the vast internet. She’s represented by Susan Raihofer.She’s the co-founder of the comedy site The Belladonna and the Satire and Humor Festival, created the online satire writing program for The Second City, and teaches workshops across the US and internationally. Her first book, New Erotica for Feminists: Satirical Fantasies of Love, Lust, and Equal Pay, was named one of the 10 best comedy books of the year. Her second, Inside Jokes: A Comedy and Creativity Guide For All Writers, is on sale now. Caitlin lives in Queens, NY with her husband, son, and neurotic husky. One of whom just pooped on the floor. ABOUT THE BOOK: Inside Jokes is a step-by-step practical guide to all types of comedy writing, filled with invaluable advice, exercises, interviews, tools, and jokes that will turn anyone into a funnier writer and person. Basically, Inside Jokes is The Artist’s Way for the funny soul.

classes.title: Workshop: You Already Did The Funny Thing with Jeff Quintana
classes.description: Workshop: You Already Did The Funny Thing with Jeff Quintana Improvisers spend so much time searching for the games that they often miss all the funny shit they've already created. In this workshop, we'll explore how the first 30 seconds of a scene can reveal multiple games through your own comedic behaviors, your connection to your scene partner, and your connection to the audience. Through specific exercises and scene work, you'll learn to recognize these patterns, discover different levels of game, and build on what's already happening instead of constantly searching for something new. Instructor Bio: Jeff Quintana is a comedian, director, educator, and creator of The Circuit Method and the S.P.E.C.S. Performance System, developed through more than 23 years of continuous performance, teaching, and research. He has trained with nearly every major school of American improvisation and has taught at The Annoyance Theatre, iO Theater, Home Comedy Theater, Brooklyn Comedy Collective, One Group Mind, and The Playground Theater. Jeff headlines nationally with The Powerful Hourful starring Antonio Quintana, Motivational Speaker, an immersive avant-clown stand-up experience that blends improvisation, audience interaction, and physical comedy into a one-of-a-kind live performance. classes.title: Drop-In: Intro to Clown w/ Tallie Medel (Tuesday, November 17th, 2026)
classes.description:
“It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

What happens in a clown class? We introduce ourselves, we have a nice long warmup, our feet get squishy and our heads get floaty, we play with tennis balls and hats, we do group games and solo exercise from some of the greats (Lecoq, Conway, Johnstone) while working on taming their ego and bringing out their true inner clown. Come to just one class, come to all of them, do what your heart desires. You’ll probably leave with a new friend.

We're in an era of cognitive dissonance, hence all this clown talk. Absurd times call for an absurd response. Clown is antifascist and you are brave!

classes.title: Improv Drop-In
classes.description: Thinking about trying improv? Our in-person drop-in classes are the perfect non-committal taste. No prior experience is necessary for these fun, relaxed introductions to some of the skills of improvised comedy. Meet new people, learn games & exercises and share 90-minutes of laughs each time you join us.

classes.title: Intro to Improv
classes.description: Looking to start your improv journey but not ready to commit to a full term of classes? Intro to Improv offers a fun and low pressure way to dive into the basics of improvisation. In this 4-week course, you’ll explore essential skills like saying “Yes, And,” making offers, and active listening. You’ll also start building trust with your ensemble and discover the joy of spontaneity and creative risk-taking. This class is designed to give you a solid foundation while fitting into your schedule.

classes.title: Public Speaking
classes.description: Do you want to become a better public speaker? Do you feel nervous, unsure or even dread when you give presentations and speeches? This class will give you the tools and skills necessary to deliver effective and engaging speeches. You will learn and practice public speaking theory in a way that is fun and challenging. This class provides participants with a theoretical foundation of public speaking along with several opportunities to practice, refine and reinforce their learning. Develop greater public speaking success professionally and personally.

classes.title: Drop-In: Intro to BCC Improv w/ Andy Junk (Thursday, November 19th, 2026)
classes.description:
This Intro class teaches you what the BCC’s approach to improv is all about - how to say both FUCK IT and LOVE IT while performing. FUCK IT means you don’t worry about the outcome or result of your efforts. You are not judging whether you perform things correctly or whether you make mistakes. You are simply committed to doing what you are doing without worrying whether it is good or not. LOVE IT means you celebrate the whimsy, joy, and delight inherent in making shit up onstage. You remember why you fell in love with improv, one of the most wonderful feelings in the world. Learn to hold both of these ideas in your head at the same time and create fearless, fun, and dumb improv.

If you are new to improv, this workshop will set you up for a fearless way to begin learning. If you are an experienced improviser, this workshop will introduce you to a new philosophy of improv that is different than other improv schools in NYC. Either way you will be challenged and motivated!

This class is designed for students new to BCC’s approach to improv.

Drop-in Class: Thursday, November 19th, 7:00PM - 9:30PM

Where: BCC DogHouse, Studio #2 (137 Montrose Ave, Brooklyn)

Each class is limited to 16 students.

classes.title: Physical Comedy Intensive: John Towsen (Saturday, November 21st, 2026)
classes.description:
In this one-day introduction to physical comedy you will be exposed to a few elements of physical comedy vocabulary involving everyday objects, learning new skills that you probably didn't even know existed. With every skill we explore, we will immediately be searching for comedy applications involving character and situation as a stepping stone to creating material. From there we will go on to exploring gag structures such as the escalating gag, the visual gag, the 3-part gag, and the oblivious gag, Participants will get to work on short pieces together since the whole point of the workshop is the integration of technique with story and character. No particular skill level, body type, or background is needed to be in the workshop, which I hope will be useful and FUN for everyone.

Intensive: Saturday, November 21st, 11:30 AM - 6:30 PM (with lunch break).

Each class is limited to 14 students.

classes.title: World Building And Connections with Frank Caeti
classes.description: You have just performed the first couple of scenes of your long form, now what? This class will focus on using scenes you have performed earlier in any long form structure to inspire new scenes, build the world, and make strong connections. Students will learn techniques like time-dash, analogous situation, theme, pattern recognition, character, location, and following the fun – are all worthwhile threads to pursue for the second beat and beyond. Prerequisite: Some improv experience helpful but not necessary. Chicago native Frank Caeti (last name rhymes with “Why Sweaty”) is an actor, writer, director, improviser, and educator. He currently works as an Assistant Teaching Professor of Theatre at Colorado State University. Frank has taught at California Institute of the Arts (CalArts), El Camino College, The Second City Conservatory Program, and other professional training centers. Frank was a series regular and contributing writer on FOX’s MADtv. His television credits include Modern Family, Key & Peele, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Chicago Fire, Reno 911, NCIS, FOX NFL Sunday, and more than 35 national commercials. Frank is an alumnus of The Second City where he performed with the National Touring Company and resident stages in Chicago and Las Vegas and has improvised at Upright Citizens Brigade, iO, and ComedySportz. His regional theater credits as an actor, writer, and director include Off-Broadway, Kennedy Center, Goodman Theatre, Kirk Douglas Theatre, La Jolla Playhouse, Laguna Playhouse, and Dallas Theater Center. As a writer, Frank has developed projects with Sony Pictures Television, written for Warner Bros. Animation, and co-created a Disney Digital web series produced by Key & Peele that was later developed for television by Sacha Baron Cohen’s Four by Two Films. He holds a BA from THE Colorado State University and an MFA from Emerson College. More info and fun video links at www.frankcaeti.com.

classes.title: Drop-In: Improvised Sketch w/ Disco Horses (Sunday, November 22nd, 2026)
classes.description:
In this class you will learn how to take the basic fundamentals of improv and work with it to generate scenes, sketches, and characters that you can take and continue to shape. Starting with the core principles of good improv; yes, and, comedic game, and world-building (who, what, where), and combining that with a basic formula for sketch writing, you will be able to start from any base or premise and lead to a functioning scene on the spot.

The course will focus on the two main points of entry of improv-to-sketch that Joe and Eric have found great success in, answering questions and understanding formula. Learning how to spot moments that will lead to better improvised scenes that lead to sketch is a skill that will come from this workshop. The class will be split into two portions. The first of which Joe and Eric will dive into their points of improv-to-sketch, and the second will be active, asking participants to practice the skills and points discussed earlier in the class.

It is recommended that you have a bit of sketch and/or improv experience (classes, performances, writing alone in your basement) before you take this workshop, however it is not required.

If you are interested in learning how to create sketches from improv efficiently and consistently, then this workshop is for you!

Workshop: Sunday, November 22nd, 3:00pm-5:30pm

Workshop limited to 14 students.

classes.title: Musical Improv Conservatory Auditions
classes.description: The Musical Improv Program is for improvisers who love creating musical scenes, and are excited to use music in their comedy career. The Second City uses songs and musical improv on all of it’s stages, and learning how to do it is a lot of fun! Students who complete this program will graduate with a deeper understanding of musical improv, approached in it’s many forms – in game play, narrative, and written work. The aim is to create improvisers who can execute these skills on a professional stage at The Second City, or anywhere else. Students in this program can expect support, encouragement, and notes to grow by. LEVELS 1 – 2 The first two levels of the music program focus on demystifying musical improv and it’s many elements, and turning them into executable and performable skills! Game play, making strong vocal and musical choices, song structures and rhyming; building musical scenes with authenticity, and building group songs in a fun and supportive environment. Shows are scheduled at each level, and a retention audition is held at the end of Level 2. LEVELS 3 – 5 The goal of Levels 3-5 is to give the student a professional level experience of musical improv training. Game play for the audience, styles and genres, and long form narratives will be explored with an eye toward re-improvisation and lyric writing. Each level will have a show, with Level 5 culminating in previews and a four-show run of a musical variety show. AUDITIONS Please come dressed comfortably for movement and ready to sing! Walk-ins may be accommodated, but are not guaranteed. Prerequisites and Eligibility A full year of improv training at The Second City is required. We will also consider a year long program at an approved school in conjunction with one Acting class post High School. Interested auditioners who have NOT completed a year of training at Second City should first submit their training information via this submission form . classes.title: Improv for Actors 1
classes.description: In today’s entertainment industry, improv and the ability to work without a script has become an essential tool not only for rehearsal, but for performance on screen and stage, as well as auditioning. Improv for Actors 1 is for people interested in how to be a better actor. IFA-1 is geared toward both working and post-grad actors who are looking to expand their craft with skills of improvisation. It’s also a great option for people with a theater degree or background in the dramatic arts to have fun with new people in a new environment. IFA-1 covers the fundamental elements of scene work, creating environment, and scenic transformation. Students acquire skills that can be applied to scripted and non-scripted work. Students become more improvisational in written moments and more confident when they improvise. Students work on building ensemble, object work, and the essence of a good improvisational scene. Using games, exercises, and other play, students explore relationships, character motivation, and heightening techniques to create compelling scenes and characters purely out of improv. Improv for Actors 1 is for students with a theater degree, currently enrolled in a full-length collegiate theater program, or have the equivalent amount of professional training and/or experience. Students must submit an acting résumé for consideration to be placed in IFA-1. Please submit a résumé through our online application.

classes.title: Intro to Acting
classes.description: The Second City Acting Program combines improvisational techniques with a variety of scripted media—including materials from the Second City archive—to help students build the foundations of grounded and compelling acting. Second City’s approach to sketch comedy is deeply rooted in behavior, relationships, character, and emotion. Over the years, our alumni have applied these principles across stage, film, and television to create performances that are not only hilarious but also heartwarming, dramatic, and award-winning. In this course, students will explore core acting techniques and methods for working with scripts. It’s a great fit for improvisers looking to refine their acting skills or for actors with little to no improv experience who want to stretch their creative muscles and expand their toolbox. Prerequisites: While some prior improv training is recommended, it is not required.

classes.description:
Love the hell out of what’s happening onstage and you’re bound to have fun and fearless improvisation.

This class will help remind you what you love about improv, slap you out of whatever may be holding you back, and cut out the naysaying voices in your head. This class will move quickly, keep you on your feet, and challenge you with personal feedback.

classes.description:
Musical improv classes at BCC are taught at an accelerated pace compared to other schools. You will be performing a fully fledged musical by the end of level 1.

You already know how to improvise, but to music? YES YOU CAN! This class will introduce improvisers with at least 1 level of experience how to create fully formed narrative musicals on the spot. We will begin each class with various rhythmic, rhyming, and listening, exercises, then delve deep into each element of narrative structure. Students will learn how to create strong protagonists, antagonists, charm scenes, and finales, while building a toolbox of musical techniques including fugues, and of course classic chorus-verse structures. Strong singing voices are not required! Just a willingness to unleash your inner diva in a joyful and supportive atmosphere.

This class culminates in a performance for the public.

Prerequisite: Completion of BCC Level 1 Improv OR students who have taken at least one full-length course at a major comedy theater (UCB, PIT, Magnet, Squirrel, Second City, iO, Annoyance, etc.) or have similar prior training can begin at this level. Please write your prior experience in the form when registering.

Note: BCC’s Musical Improv 1 culminates in a full-length Improvised Musical so we require a prerequisite of a full-length Improv 1 class. Our musical improv classes move at a faster pace compared to most other theaters' programs. This is an advanced class, so we do not allow skipping to Musical Improv 2. Trust us, you will be challenged :)

classes.description: CRASS2: Sketch To Narrative Play CRASS (CReating Annoyance Style Shows) is a the next step in The Annoyance's process; using improv to create written material. The Annoyance has enjoyed pushing the envelope of what plays and musicals can be. With this class, students will continue their journey of turning their improv into written works, now adding the complexity of a narrative play through it all. classes.title: Clown Level 1: Welcome to Clown Town w/ Hannah Mitchell (Jan-Feb '27) (Tuesday)
classes.description:
Clown. The great equalizer.

"It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

Clown trains us to be fully present. Class curriculum includes exercises from Jacques Lecoq, Jean Taylor, Merry Conway, Nader Farman, Keith Johnstone and more, aiming to move us past ego and toward our shared humanity. Winter is coming. But class is joyful and warm! Come on out, try on the red nose.

Recognize the universal shared experience that is clowning.

This class culminates in a public class performance.

classes.title: Writing 1
classes.description: Writing 1 is for any student who is looking to start the journey of writing to and for a Second City-style revue. This class is the foundation for scenic comedy writing, a guide for utilizing an improviser’s skill set for rapid creation, and learning writing refinement. The concepts and tools provided in Writing 1 are the building blocks for being able to quickly and creatively write to and for a Second City-style revue. Every comedic writer must have the knowledge and skills that are offered in this course. Writing 1 teaches students how to write comedic scenes that could be found in a Second City-style revue by exploring different scenic set-ups, character dialogue, genres and point-of-view. Students use improv as a tool for character and dialogue generation. Writing 1 class time includes a combination of solo exercises and collaborative exercises to build skills in brainstorming, comedic structure and character development. Students also gain a Second City perspective on theatrical writing – including observation, idea generation, dialogue, and character creation. Feedback focuses on ‘what works’ in terms of the structural building blocks. Class time is active, positive and encouraging. Students practice concepts through a series of weekly homework assignments. Any student interested in creating Second City-style comedic writing or interested in extending their improvisation abilities and experiences into writing should take Writing 1.

Writing 1 teaches students how to write comedic scenes that could be found in a Second City-style revue by exploring different scenic set-ups, character dialogue, genres and point-of-view. Students use improv as a tool for character and dialogue generation. Writing 1 class time includes a combination of solo exercises and collaborative exercises to build skills in brainstorming, comedic structure and character development. Students also gain a Second City perspective on theatrical writing – including observation, idea generation, dialogue, and character creation. Feedback focuses on ‘what works’ in terms of the structural building blocks. Class time is active, positive and encouraging. Students practice concepts through a series of weekly homework assignments. Any student interested in creating Second City-style comedic writing or interested in extending their improvisation abilities and experiences into writing should take Writing 1.

AP1 introduces you to Chicago's approach to improv by covering a wide variety of concepts:​ The rules of Improv and breaking the rules Group mind (the myth, the facts) How to say "yes, and" and when to say “no” Finding or Creating the game Long-form Short-form Writing via improv Direction (taking and giving) Object and environment work Introducing a show This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term. classes.title: AP2 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description: AP2: Beginning Annoyance Philosophy - Initiations AP2 is an immersive examination of The Annoyance philosophy on, and approach to, improv. AP2 focuses on decisive initiations and a strong point of view. This class focuses on the first seconds of scenes and explores how they affect the rest of the scene. In AP2, you will cover: Personal responsibility in a scene − taking care of yourself and your choices Trusting instincts Creating/Finding “Your Deal” at the top of the scene Beginning character development Object work as inspiration Environment as inspiration The responsibility of operating without censorship. Individual feedback and tendencies This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term. Prerequisite: AP1 or sufficient background in improv. Please let us know in the comments section below where you have studied so that we may contact them to confirm.

classes.title: AP3 - Sundays withTBD T127
classes.description: AP3: Scene Work AP3 is about taking that next step in scenes. While AP2 focused on the beginning moments of a scene, in AP3 students are challenged to play with more complexity and style, juggling it all within a scene while always maintaining their strong point of view. Aspects of this class include: Acknowledging the realities of your scene partner Scenic development: Finding the Highways and Bi-ways of a scene to extend its length Managing context without getting in your head (the who/what/where/when/why/etc.) Creating specific, surprising choices Playing with Opposites and Curve Balls Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene In-depth three person and group scene work Protecting and Playing the Freak Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working Managing forms and style DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”) Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool. Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback Prerequisite : Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.

classes.title: AP4 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description: AP4 Through individual feedback, setting performance goals, and identifying and breaking habits, AP4 offers fine-tuning and involves the following aspects: Stretching the performer Pushing unique specificity Keeping voice in multiple person scenes, split-scenes Making rich, varied environments Embodying the character and embellishing the world Organic improv ∼ developing a scene based on physical and emotional choices Prerequisite: Students must have completed AP3 to take this class.

classes.title: CRASS1 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description: CRASS1: Improv to Sketch CRASS (CReating Annoyance Style Shows) is a the next step in The Annoyance's process; using improv to create written material. In CRASS 1, students will take all of the improv skills they've honed in AP1-5 and together with their director, create a written sketch revue. Students will be assigned additional roles outside of actor/writer and may be responsible for costumes, props, etc. These classes are more intensive than AP1-5 and will require additional work and rehearsal outside of class hours. For over 30 years the Annoyance has specialized in using improv comedy to create full length plays and musicals. From Annoyance classics like Splatter Theater and Co-ed Prison Sluts, to more modern shows like Steamworks: The Musical and Live Laugh Blood, The Annoyance has enjoyed pushing the envelope of what plays and musicals can be. With this class, students will start the journey of turning their improv into written works, refining, planning, and creating a full sketch revue. classes.title: SUMMER INTENSIVE 2027
classes.description: The iO Summer Intensive Program meets every Monday through Thursday from 11am to 5pm for five weeks from July 5th through August 5th 2027. EARLY BIRD PRICING: Full Program for $1,700 through March 31st, 2027 Price Increases to $1,800 on April 1st, 2027 Unlike anything you'll ever experience! Spend 5 weeks at the historic iO Theater in Chicago, the birthplace of improvisation, learning long form in its greatest incubator from the world's greatest comedy teachers. The iO Summer Intensive condenses five levels of our curriculum into five weeks. The class meets every Monday through Thursday from 11am to 5pm for five weeks. Each week, you'll work with a different iO teaching artist on a particular level of curriculum. Best of all, the class culminates in a performance here in our theater! Week 1 is Level 1 – Ensemble – Introduces the basics of agreement, making strong choices, supporting your partner, exploring pattern, heightening, and intro to long-form. Week 2 is Level 2 – The Performer’s Skill Set – Focuses on advanced character work and exploring environment, using exercises and games designed to take the improviser out of their head and into the character and the world onstage. Object work, physical investment in character choices, wants & objectives, and advanced listening exercises Week 3 is Level 3 – Scene Work – Extensive work in two-person improvised scenes sharpens listening skills, emotional choices, and investment in the dynamics of a scene, such as status and “game”. Introduction to editing techniques, tag-outs, walk-ons, and further work with iO’s signature form, The Harold. Week 4 is Level 4 – Long-form – Incorporating skills learned throughout the previous levels, focus is on building character, relationship, and form with emphasis on grounded scene work as the foundation for long-forms. Week 5 is Level 5 – Form Creation – Applies the skills from Levels 1-4 to create your own piece. The class focuses on the structure, including openings, group games, and scenes. Advanced pattern work, group work, editing, and scene work are used to explore the challenges and magic of long-form. Students have class shows in addition to weekly class sessions. Come learn at the best improv theater in the world all while making new friends in one of the best cities in the world! All Summer Intensive Students will receive an iO Student ID which gets you access to all regular shows for free! It also gets you discount tickets at some other improv theaters in the city. For 2027, the Summer Intensive will begin on July 5th and culminate in a performance here at the iO. The program will cost $1800. (Convenience fees are added for purchases made via credit card.
